idea-plugin.name: Marginalis
idea-plugin.description:
Margin conversations between you and your AI coding agent — Google Docs comments over live code, built for the review loop, not the keystroke loop.

Marginalis is deliberately turn-based: your agent never types over your shoulder. While you work, it reads the margin and leaves replies, review findings, and guided walkthroughs anchored to the exact lines — even the exact words — they are about. Threads survive edits and restarts, carry per-agent read receipts ("the agent will see this next turn" is a promise, not a hope), and resolve only when their outcome actually lands in code.

  • Anchored threads — comment on a line, or select the exact words (Alt+Shift+M); anchors track edits and re-find their content after restarts instead of drifting.
  • Turn signals — editor-tab glyphs, gutter badges, and a tool-window count answer "is it my turn?" at a glance; a balloon arrives when the agent posts in a file you don't have open.
  • Severity as a gate — the agent marks findings blocker ("act before this proceeds") or nit ("dismiss guilt-free"); filter the tree to what actually gates the merge.
  • Guided walkthroughs — the agent numbers steps through a change ("look here 1st, 2nd, …"); walk them with the next/previous-occurrence shortcuts, resolve as you go, step totals stay stable.
  • A review protocol, not just comments — resolved means the outcome is in the code; read receipts are per agent, so several agents (one designing, one implementing) share a margin without consuming each other's unread.
  • Agent-agnostic transport — plain JSON over the IDE's built-in HTTP server; anything that can make an HTTP request can converse. No MCP server, no extra configuration.

Threads persist per project (.idea/marginalis.json), so the conversation is part of the workspace, not the session. Apache-2.0, source on GitHub.

action.description: Start a margin thread on the current line — or on the selected text — for the agent to pick up
